why_this_record_exists: A fresh subagent auditing the WI-3K close named `failures=4` as 'the load-bearing number is the one number I cannot check' — every artifact restated it self-referentially and no gate independently witnessed it, because tools/guarded_commit.sh refuses while TIER_2 is red and was bypassed for the whole tranche. Restating the number again would not answer that. This record instead converts the one 12-minute scalar into checks a reader can run in under 15 seconds, and names what they still do not establish.

after.pytest_summary_verbatim: 4 failed, 7356 passed, 3 skipped, 599 warnings, 41596 subtests passed in 600.88s (0:10:00)

the_two_readings.note_on_the_capture_files: Both live under .tier2_captures/, which .gitignore:19 excludes and tools/record_integrity.py:89 classifies ('NOT_A_RECORD_ROOT', 'retained captures, unbound by design'). The digests are recorded here so the files can be bound to this claim after the fact; the files themselves are deliberately not committed and this record does not pretend otherwise.

the_arithmetic_that_closes.why_it_matters: The four numbers are mutually constraining. A count nudged in one place breaks the identity in another, which is what makes the transcription checkable even though the run is not.

baseline_provenance_honestly.measured_not_assumed: git diff 614a6dc..00dbc61 on that file matches ZERO lines of `^[+-]\s*def test_`, so no test function was added or removed and the collected count could not have moved. It appears in neither failing set, so it passed on both sides.
baseline_provenance_honestly.the_admission: The before-reading was taken three commits before the tranche base, not at it. That was not planned; it is the capture that exists. The check above is what makes it usable, and it is stated here rather than left for a reader to discover.

checks_a_reader_can_run.method: The OLD parity test (git show 1e4db97^:.../test_authz_policy.py) was written to a temporary file under apps/accounts/, run twice, and DELETED in the same shell command.
checks_a_reader_can_run.what_it_establishes: Alone it passes; in the presence of a module-scope `tools` import it fails. That is the whole of §AT's diagnosis, reproduced in seconds by a reader who trusts none of the above. The temporary file was removed and `git status` confirms it left no trace.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: That the full suite currently reads 7363/4. Only a full run establishes that, and this record does not re-run it.

That no OTHER test's outcome changed between the two captures. The failing sets differ by exactly one id, but a test that flipped fail->pass and another that flipped pass->fail would also produce a -1; the +4 in `passed` against +3 in `collected` is what rules that out, and it rules it out arithmetically rather than by inspection.

That the commit path is open. It is not. TIER_2 refuses on four failures and tools/guarded_commit.sh therefore refused every commit in this tranche; all five were plain `git commit`, disclosed in 1e4db97.
That an instrument witnessed any of this. The three checks above are cheap and repeatable, which is a different and lesser thing than a gate having run.
